axes.name: Original obligations and negative constraints
axes.finding: Material issue present: M1. All original brief context/outcomes/boundaries and unresolved inputs are addressed in the final except the explicit plan reversibility comparison. Original 60-minute request is separately not demonstrated as elapsed time; early-completion stage mechanics are disclosed. Final excludes heat/solvents/destructive collection sampling/removal, archival-advertising safety and lifetime extrapolation.

axes.name: Consequential source claims: subject, operation, version, defaults, units, type, domain and exceptions
axes.finding: No remaining material scientific claim error found. Independently verified governing primary study/specification conditions, including print-model scope, RH-cycle method, permanent adhesion, ribbon/curved-surface qualifications, local seasonal monitoring and HDPE-specific evidence. Candidate maps have minor dates/operation precision issues. Numeric 15-min/six-coupon/12-week choices are proposed operational choices, not borrowed source defaults.

axes.name: Useful unfamiliar discovery, competing/analogous approaches, implementation/history and opportunity breadth
axes.finding: Discovery is substantive: drying restraint/moisture transients, delayed ink co-solvent curl, printer-specific housing systems, low-energy sleeve interface, mechanical retention and observation-first practice. Records requests discriminate simultaneous supply/printer changes and identify lot/formulation/work-instruction history. Final preserves the monitoring alternative and technical breadth, but does not substantively carry the requested reversibility comparison/mechanical evaluation through its decision study (M1). No requirement for a brand winner or unidentified supplier history is invented.

axes.name: Wrong criticism/corrections/rejections and exact plan dispositions
axes.finding: All four criticisms have explicit final dispositions and were independently adjudicated. I-1 is a useful contingent clarification rather than proof that original brief required a sleeve factorial; I-2/I-4 corrections are sound; I-3 uncertainty was appropriate for mapped packets. No empirical product rejection or fabricated tested result. However the Plan meaningful-alternatives Covered disposition overstates reversibility coverage (M1). Full exact-clause ledger independently records this rather than accepting stage labels.

axes.name: Supported meaning preserved through discovery/draft/critique/final
axes.finding: Core conditional mechanisms, system/history records, separate endpoints, monitoring, consent/unknowns and proposed-only status survive. Original commercial-pulp and unsupported-duration/sleeve-scope issues are corrected or qualified. Discovery’s conditional coupon-heating permission is excluded in the final. Mechanical-attachment comparison substance is compressed and required reversibility remains unoperationalized (M1); agreement and stable hashes do not cure this.

axes.name: Meaningful proposed versus executed validation and oracle applicability
axes.finding: Proposed validation is largely discriminating: compatible staged contrasts, sleeve strata, reference/unprinted/bare controls, repeated measurements at conditioned reference, independent outcomes and predeclared owner gates. No actual case performance was tested. Six coupons do not certify rare failures; seasonal monitoring does not validate adhesion; 12 weeks is a cap with an inconclusive outcome. Reversibility has no prospective comparison/oracle in the final despite the exact plan requirement (M1). Other material identities/thresholds legitimately remain external after necessary desk investigation.

material_findings.title: Required reversibility comparison is asserted covered but absent from the final decision study
material_findings.exact_obligation: Compare reversibility and annotation preservation as well as apparent adhesion.

prior_supported_locators.section: Alternatives and history that discriminate causes

material_findings.observation: The final names replaceability and whether mechanical retention is workable as owner choices, and cites NARA’s permanent/difficult-to-remove adhesive. Its prospective measurements/gates nevertheless contain only dimensions, bond failure, readability, identity and contact risk. It supplies neither a comparison of reversibility nor an explicit prospective reversibility question/assessment for the candidate and retain-current/nonadhesive options. Reversibility appears as a claimed covered gate only in the clause register. A bond peel measurement and spontaneous lift/ooze recording do not themselves compare whether a label/retention method can be undone while preserving the sleeve and original information.
material_findings.materiality: This is an explicit original plan criterion for choosing among attachment approaches, not an invented requirement to use a reversible adhesive or remove collection labels. NARA’s specification values permanent attachment whereas the NMS guidance distinguishes secure attachment from reversibility. An option can meet the final’s stated bond/legibility gates while leaving that requested tradeoff unassessed. The decision study therefore cannot support its claim that all exact plan clauses are covered.
material_findings.external_choice_distinction: The owner may still decide whether replacement/removability is required, and no universal reversibility threshold or performance test is required now. The missing element is the requested research comparison and how that unresolved requirement bears on choosing an approach. Merely leaving replaceability open does not perform that comparison.
material_findings.lineage: The investigator discovered removable loop/tag/insert/secondary-enclosure options and a separate mock-up with visibility, retrieval, snagging, handling and misassociation checks. The final retains an environmental alternative well, but compresses mechanical retention to a tag citation and claimed mock-up in the register; it does not preserve the substantive alternative evaluation. The earlier draft itself only weakly operationalized reversibility, so this is both an unresolved plan omission and a loss of supported alternative substance.
material_findings.conclusion: Source-backed FAIL for full-pipeline qualification. No candidate repair or feedback was provided.
material_findings.materiality_inference: This is a reviewer inference from the explicit plan criterion, the complete final measurement/gate text, and primary guidance/specification distinctions. No actual sleeve or product was observed to fail.

limitations.text: All stage maps describe S05/S06 as having no displayed date. Independent official pages show S05 Page details 2021-02-05, and S06 a 2018 publication/catalog/ISBN plus Page details 2025-12-02. This does not overturn the environmental or paper-mechanics claim.

The carried S07 maps conflate 24-hour peel and loop tack as 24-hour peel/tack. Primary methods distinguish delayed peel from loop tack. The final does not use these numerical findings and explicitly preserves its own retrieval uncertainty.

The final is a research proposal with no actual case specimens, product identities, supplier records, environmental trace or acceptable failure limits. These honestly remain external prerequisites; they are not additional failures.

The original brief’s full 60-minute duration was not demonstrated. Archived native/T3 timestamps describe a shorter completed staged pipeline; exact effective research occupancy is UNKNOWN. Staged assignments also expressly permit early completion. Do not convert this into a semantic falsehood or billing/speed claim.

No case-specific product reformulation or implementation failure report can be established for unidentified supplies. The proposal gives substantive dated specifications, paper manufacturing/process mechanisms and future batch-record leads. Unknown products do not justify inventing a winner, history, lifetime or deployment.

unknowns: Actual store stock/adhesive/printer/sleeve identity and condition, humidity history, failure denominator, acceptable failure rate, annotation-copy/replaceability authority and resources.
An informative coupon exposure/duration and reversibility criterion for the eventual identified system; no actual material performance or lifetime is known.
Independent authentication/freshness of candidate native receipts and exact pre-input call order; full original tool traces were not in mapped science packet and no history was accessed.
Effective provider/model/reasoning/service tier beyond requested-route/archived T3 identity fields; effective inference/research occupancy, retries/queue attribution, billable usage and cost.
Recipe-wide sealing/release authority or state of other C inputs, arms, assessments, outcome labels or ER11; deliberately not read or inferred.

critic_dispositions.independent_disposition: Reasonable clarification/design strengthening; categorical materiality is conditional on multiple relevant sleeve surfaces, not an obligation to vary every factor.
critic_dispositions.analysis: The original draft already specified spare same-lot or documented matching sleeves and discussed sleeve identity; it could hold a verified substrate fixed. It did not make a multi-sleeve stratum/scope rule explicit. The final adds blocks, no pooling, single-stratum applicability and explicit uncovered strata. This is valid and does not establish a sleeve cause or require an unsupported universal matrix.

The primary paper methods do not justify a 12-week label-system durability or discriminating horizon. The original draft called its 12 weeks exploratory but lacked the final’s explicit cap/adequacy distinction and inconclusive/extension rule. The final states the sources do not establish adequate duration, retains 12 weeks only as a feasibility-approved planning maximum, and gives informative-exposure/nonresponse/lot-conflict limits. Matrix scale is staged; no assumed volunteer resource limit is imposed. Remaining duration/cap choice is honestly external, not a material scientific error.

critic_dispositions.independent_disposition: Appropriate for the mapped critic/reviser packet. Reviewer can corroborate additional archived timing facts without rewriting their science.
critic_dispositions.analysis: Critic/reviser input maps omit investigator activation receipts and timing assignment; the final accurately avoids asserting full-window compliance. This assessment has independently read the original assignment/freeze and stored native receipts, which corroborate the quoted stage deadline and a reported 928-second Goal. Receipt provenance/effective occupancy remains limited. Time is reported separately; retaining uncertainty is not a false criticism or a science repair.

S01 used laboratory sheets prepared from commercial pulps, not finished commercially manufactured sheets. Final wording accurately restores the exact experimental subject. Original imprecision remains in discovery/draft lineage and does not invalidate the qualified final claim.

sources.title: Changes in the macro and nano-structure of paper during moisture cycling
sources.source_locator: Abstract; Experimental: sample sheet preparation and hygroexpansion measurements; Results: restrained/free drying; E01.txt lines 19, 48–71, 91–108, 183–185
sources.exact_subject: Non-directional laboratory sheets prepared from four commercial softwood pulps, with varying refining, pressing and drying restraint
sources.independently_observed_operation: Read publisher methods/results independently. Four RH cycles 50→20→90→50%, 23 °C, ≥24 h at each level; ≥5 strain specimens and ≥4 moisture-ratio specimens per paper.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Study measurements, not a label/storage default. Restrained-drying sheets showed irreversible shrinkage; freely dried sheets less so. No label adhesive/sleeve test and no storage-life conversion.
sources.applicability: Supports conditional dimensional-change and manufacturing-history hypotheses. Does not diagnose the case or justify its coupon duration.
sources.assessment: Final claim supported; earlier commercial-pulp-sheet wording clarified correctly.
sources.successful_access_method: Independent direct HTTPS capture plus semantic reading of relevant surrounding primary text.

sources.title: Long term curl of printing paper due to ink solvent migration
sources.version_or_release: Published article; online 2023-12-20; Materials & Design 237 (2024), 112593; DOI 10.1016/j.matdes.2023.112593
sources.exact_subject: Two industrial office-paper grades, sized/unsized; model ink, not the store’s unidentified printing system
sources.independently_observed_operation: Read primary PDF methods/results. One-sided spray of approximately 10 g/m² of 60 wt% glycerol/40 wt% water; pure-water comparison; curl and through-thickness glycerol through 168 h, with storage at 23 °C/50% RH.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Short-term 10 sheets/grade; long-term figures 3 sheets/grade. Migration and curl continued after one week; results do not establish another printer technology, bond behavior or lifetime.
sources.applicability: Conditional print/process mechanism and ordinary versus model-test distinction are sound; source cannot support a universal 12-week endpoint.
sources.assessment: Final model/process qualification supported. Surrounding paper also discusses structural and roll-set curl; these are additional leads, not extra case obligations.
sources.successful_access_method: Independent direct HTTPS capture plus semantic reading of relevant surrounding primary text.

sources.title: NARA RXC laser-print pressure-sensitive label specification
sources.version_or_release: October 2015; revision note identifies a new specification
sources.source_locator: PDF pp. 1–3, Scope, II.1.B Adhesive, II.2 Bond Strength, Other Label Properties, Workmanship, QC; E03.txt lines 6–44, 52–70, 119–134
sources.exact_subject: Procured laser-print paper/acrylic-adhesive labels for paper/board/plastic/metal housings and metal furniture
sources.independently_observed_operation: Read all three pages and visually checked p.1. Printer/toner/configuration are procurement-selected. The specified 90° modified ASTM D2860/D2860M-04 Procedure B uses 1×2.5 in sample supporting 200 g for 10 min.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Explicitly excludes direct application to documents/records. Adhesive is permanent and difficult to remove. Bond, print/scanner readability, flatness and lot QC are distinct; no case default.
sources.applicability: Correctly used as a system/specification lead rather than a safety certification. Permanence establishes why attachment success is not a reversibility comparison.
sources.assessment: Final factual claim supported; evidence relevant to M1.
sources.successful_access_method: Independent direct HTTPS capture plus semantic reading of relevant surrounding primary text.

sources.title: NARA RXC thermal-transfer pressure-sensitive label specification
sources.version_or_release: October 2015 revision of May 2013, previously reformatted September 2010
sources.source_locator: PDF pp. 1–3, Scope/curved-surface note, II.1, II.2, II.3.B, QC/revision note; E04.txt lines 6–45, 53–60, 111–116
sources.exact_subject: Specified thermal-transfer label systems for housings/furniture; polyester or polypropylene film face stock/acrylic adhesive/polyester liner
sources.independently_observed_operation: Read all three pages and visually checked p.1. Polypropylene preferred for curved substrates, either film for flat surfaces. Hard-resin ribbon required; wax/wax-resin excluded. Same 200 g/10 min/1×2.5 in/90° bond criterion.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Printer/ribbon/configuration selected in procurement; adhesive permanent and difficult to remove. Does not establish conservation safety, handwriting performance or compatibility with the case sleeve.
sources.applicability: Supports process/material/version-history inquiry, not a product selection or borrowed test threshold.
sources.assessment: Final claim supported; permanence also relevant to M1.

sources.title: Modified Acrylate Pressure-Sensitive Adhesives for Low-Surface-Energy Substrate and Adhesion Mechanism Models
sources.source_locator: Independent full-text PMC mirror: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12073116/ ; Abstract, §§2.4–2.5, §3.5, Conclusions, COI; E07.txt lines 61–70, 108–116, 366–382
sources.exact_subject: HHTPB-modified acrylic PSA tapes on HDPE in controlled laboratory adhesion tests
sources.independently_observed_operation: Retrieved article independently through direct HTTPS PMC after web challenge. PET-backed adhesive approximately 25 g/m²; peel 150×25 mm at 300 mm/min after 20 min/24 h, five passes of 2 kg roller, triplicate means; loop tack a separate 125×25 mm test.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Abstract reports 24 h peel 4.88 N/25 mm and loop tack 8.14 N/25 mm at 20 °C and decreasing peel with temperature. Loop tack is not a 24-hour peel test. Industry co-author disclosed. No conservation/long-storage proof.
sources.applicability: Valid conditional surface/interface lead. Final’s unverified-by-reviser qualification is honest, even though this reviewer could verify the primary article. Detailed results are not used to choose a material.
sources.assessment: Final supported; carried maps’ phrase 24-hour peel/tack compresses distinct operations (minor lineage/source-map issue).
sources.identity_same_article_basis: Same DOI, title and PMID; no silent source-ID rebinding.
